data.narrative:
Zeta Surgical is a seed-stage biotech company that has raised $9M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparison universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-sector companies including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Chai Discovery.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the company's $9M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of the seed-to-next-stage transition in biotech, yielding an implied valuation of $22M. Peer-median analysis was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds (0 of 3 required datapoints). Public-comp anchoring could not be applied because the target company does not disclose revenue, limiting the utility of the 6.6x median price-to-sales multiple observed across public peers.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $19M to $26M, with a median point of $22M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed financials or product-stage milestones that might justify upside or downside adjustments relative to peer trajectories, and the thinness of directly comparable seed-stage biotech datapoints in the current dataset.
